title: SRN Members Sweep Top 3 at West Africa Sim Racing Cup
excerpt: Chidi Okonkwo led a dominant Nigerian clean-sweep in the inaugural WASC, taking pole, fastest lap, and victory in the final round at Monza.
body: Nigeria arrived at the inaugural West Africa Sim Racing Cup as the team to beat, and left with every step of the podium. Chidi Okonkwo topped qualifying at Monza by three tenths, converted it into a lights-to-flag win, and set the fastest lap of the race for good measure.

Behind him, fellow SRN drivers filled out second and third, giving the community its first clean-sweep at a regional event. The result caps a season in which SRN drivers have steadily climbed the West African rankings.
Organizers have confirmed the Cup will return next season with a full six-round calendar, and SRN is already fielding a wider driver roster for the expanded format.
author: SRN Editorial

title: How to Build a Competitive Sim Rig for Under ₦500k
excerpt: Our definitive guide to sourcing wheels, pedals, and rigs locally.
body: A common question in the SRN newcomer channel: what does it actually take to get race-ready without importing everything piece by piece? This guide breaks down a build that keeps total cost under ₦500,000 while staying competitive in club racing.

The short version: prioritize the wheelbase and pedals over the monitor setup, buy a rig frame rather than building one from scratch unless you enjoy the project, and lean on the community marketplace for lightly used gear before ordering new.
Full parts list, local supplier notes, and a step-by-step assembly walkthrough are maintained in the community resources hub.
author: Bola Afolabi

title: Season 4 2026 Drops: What Nigerian Racers Need to Know
excerpt: New content, track updates, and how SRN drivers are preparing.
body: This season's build brings a handful of track updates and a new car to the fixed-setup ladder — welcome news for drivers who've been climbing the license ranks over the past year.
SRN is running a dedicated practice league for the first two weeks of the season to help members get comfortable with the changes before jumping into official races.
author: Tunde Adeyemi

title: SRN Lagos Meetup Recap: 60 Drivers, One Track
excerpt: A look back at our biggest real-world gathering yet.
body: Sixty drivers, a dozen rigs, and one very loud viewing room — the SRN Lagos meetup was the largest in-person gathering the community has hosted. Members brought their own wheels and pedals to swap onto shared rigs, turning the afternoon into an informal gear-testing session as much as a race day.
A live bracket ran on the main screen throughout, with the eventual winner taking home a set of donated pedals from a local sim racing retailer.
Plans for a Abuja edition are already underway for later this year.
author: Adaeze Nwosu

title: Inside the SRN Newcomer Mentor Program
excerpt: How the community pairs first-time racers with mentors for their first ten races.
body: Starting competitive sim racing cold can be intimidating — unfamiliar rating systems, incident points, and race etiquette all at once. The newcomer mentor program pairs each new member with an experienced racer for their first ten official races.
Since launching, the program has onboarded dozens of drivers, several of whom have gone on to podium in their first club series.
author: Ifeoma Chukwu

title: ACC Endurance Series Round 3: A Podium in the Rain
excerpt: Adaeze Nwosu came home third after a late-race downpour reshuffled the order.
body: A dry forecast turned into a soaked final stint at round 3 of the community ACC Endurance Series, catching several front-runners out on slick tyres. Adaeze Nwosu, who had pitted early for wets on a hunch, came through the chaos to finish third.
The result moves her up to second in the endurance standings with two rounds remaining.
author: SRN Editorial

title: A Setup Guide for the Formula Pro Class
excerpt: Bola Afolabi shares the baseline setup SRN drivers are using in rFactor 2.
body: rFactor 2's Formula Pro class rewards a stable rear end more than outright downforce, which trips up drivers coming over from other sims. This guide walks through the baseline setup the SRN rFactor 2 group has converged on this season.
Expect a follow-up covering wet-weather adjustments once the current dry-only rotation ends.
author: Bola Afolabi

title: New Community Livery Pack for the Touring Car Mod
excerpt: Emeka Eze releases a fresh set of liveries for the SRN touring car community mod.
body: Twelve new liveries, each inspired by a different Nigerian state, are now available for the community touring car mod. Emeka Eze, who leads the livery project, says a second pack focused on sponsor-style designs is already in progress.
author: Emeka Eze
